name: Luxembourg
tagline: A fortress city on a gorge, a wine river, and free public transport across the whole country.
summary: Luxembourg is 2,586 square kilometres, trilingual by default, and richer per head than almost anywhere. The capital sits on a rock split by two river valleys, with casemates tunnelled through it. In 2020 it made all public transport free nationwide, which turns out to be the single best reason to travel around it slowly.

season.note: The Moselle harvest in September and October is the highlight of the year. Summer is green and walkable in the Mullerthal. The capital empties at weekends, which makes it pleasant.

getting_around: All public transport — train, tram, bus — is free for everyone, resident or not. The country is crossable in ninety minutes.
food: Judd mat Gaardebounen: smoked pork collar with broad beans
Moselle Riesling and Crémant, both underrated because nobody exports them
Gromperekichelcher, potato fritters, from a market stall
know: Free public transport applies to second class on every line in the country.
Luxembourgish is the national language; French runs administration and German runs the press.
Cross-border commuters nearly double the capital's population on weekdays.

regions.name: The Capital & the Moselle
regions.summary: The fortress city, and the vineyard river that forms the German border.

cities.name: Luxembourg City
cities.summary: A UNESCO-listed fortress on cliffs, with 17 kilometres of tunnels underneath and a modern quarter on the plateau above.
highlights: The Bock casemates, cut into the rock from 1644
The Chemin de la Corniche, called Europe's most beautiful balcony
The Grund at the bottom of the gorge, reached by a free lift

experiences.name: Into the Bock casemates
experiences.summary: Kilometres of gun galleries in the cliff; they sheltered 35,000 people in 1944 and are cold in any weather.

cities.name: Remich & the Moselle
cities.summary: Terraced vineyards on a slow river, with Germany on the far bank and Crémant cellars on this one.
highlights: Crémant tasting where it is bottled
The riverside cycle path along both banks

regions.name: Mullerthal & the Ardennes
regions.summary: Sandstone ravines in the east, and castle country in the wooded north.

cities.name: Echternach
cities.summary: The country's oldest town, with a 7th-century abbey and a hopping procession on the UNESCO list.
highlights: The Mullerthal Trail through sandstone clefts and moss
The dancing procession, every Whit Tuesday since the Middle Ages

experiences.name: Little Switzerland on foot
experiences.summary: 112 km of waymarked trail through gorges narrow enough to touch both walls; a day section is easy and free.

cities.name: Vianden
cities.summary: A restored hilltop castle above a river village, where Victor Hugo spent his exile.
highlights: The castle, one of the largest west of the Rhine
Hugo's house on the bridge, kept as it was
The chairlift up for the view back
